A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying research, renamed from SCILLA to ViiNeuS. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original reconstruction experiments on four driving datasets, computational measurements, ablations, and additional Tanks and Temples experiments.

after.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction experiments and ablations on four driving datasets, including newly reported Gaussian Opacity Fields comparisons.

M1.justification: Despite the rename, the proposed architecture, joint density/SDF prediction, proposal-network sampling, three-stage initialization, sample attribution, gradient normalization, and losses remain unchanged. Expanded initialization explanations do not introduce a different procedure.

E1.justification: v4 removes the Tanks and Temples experiments from v3 Section 11.1 and Figure 10, covering Auditorium, Temple, Truck, and Meetingroom. This eliminates all demonstrated indoor and non-driving coverage. The same sixteen scenes across the four driving datasets remain.

E2.justification: v4 adds Gaussian Opacity Fields (GOF), with sparse and dense initialization variants, to the quantitative comparisons across all four driving datasets, efficiency measurements, and qualitative comparisons. StreetSurf, COLMAP, OpenMVS, and the appendix Neuralangelo comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new GOF experiments introduce sparse-versus-dense point-cloud initialization and a rasterizer adjustment for off-center camera intrinsics (Section 4.3). The proposed method's stated training schedule, driving-scene selections, sampling intervals, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. The numerical revisions do not establish that these retained protocols changed.

E4.justification: The Tanks and Temples comparison with and without hybrid initialization is removed. The convergence ablation also changes: the cyan trajectories exchange SDF/density assignments between v3 Figure 6a and v4 Figure 5a. The driving component ablations, hybrid-duration analysis, sample-attribution study, and three illustrated failure cases remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard-deviation bands across four sequences per driving dataset. These plots move from v3 Figure 4 to v4 appendix Figure 7 without a new uncertainty-estimation practice. Neither version reports additional repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises many existing scores: the proposed method's KITTI-360 Seq. 31 P-to-M changes from 0.15 to 0.11 m, and COLMAP's Pandaset Seq. 43 precision changes from 0.31 to 0.63. GOF accuracy and resource results are added, while Tanks and Temples results disappear. The convergence plot also reverses the cyan curves' method assignments. The PDFs do not explain the existing-score revisions as algorithmic improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, rendering and loss equations, and appendix gradient-normalization derivation remain equivalent. The added SDF-initialization paragraph provides conceptual motivation and a citation, without introducing a theorem, proof, or revised formal assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions explicitly focus on SDF initialization from street views with limited image overlap. The contribution list replaces the regularization contribution with extensive SDF/MVS benchmarking. The central hybrid-initialization, reconstruction-quality, and twofold training-speed claims remain.

C2.justification: v4 links the density-learning rationale more specifically to limited overlap and partial observability, acknowledges MVS recovery of finer structures, and adds explanations of GOF failures involving sky, empty space, and driving-camera configurations. The non-driving applicability discussion is removed; the three stated limitations of the proposed method remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 describes the GPU as RTX4090-equivalent, documents GOF implementation adaptations and its timing breakdown, explicitly mentions pedestrian masking in Pandaset, and describes Blender video generation. Existing architecture, optimizer, loss-weight, hash-grid, camera-selection, and frame-sampling details are retained. These disclosures do not establish reruns of existing experiments.

R1.justification: v4 adds discussion and citations for SuGaR, 2D Gaussian Splatting, GOF, and Yariv et al. (2020), strengthening positioning around Gaussian reconstruction and SDF initialization. The Tanks and Temples citation is removed. OpenMVS remains the evaluated baseline, although its v4 citation points to an OpenMVG reference.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming SCILLA to ViiNeuS and changing the title, v4 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contribution list, related work, and several method/results passages around limited image overlap. It also reorganizes ablation discussion and appendix subsections, removes the Tanks and Temples application section, and adds a supplementary-video section.

P2.justification: The qualitative montages are extensively rebuilt with GOF columns, different views, redistributed scenes, and removal of RGB reference columns and highlighted boxes. Tables 1 and 2 expand, cumulative-error plots move to the appendix, and the Tanks and Temples figure is removed. Several retained supplementary figures are regrouped after the references.

improvement.justification: The GOF comparisons and clearer initialization-focused motivation strengthen evaluation and framing. However, v4 introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Table 1 gives 0.11 m for KITTI-360 Seq. 31 while Table 3 retains 0.15 m; both reported 0.15 m in v3. The cyan SDF/density curve assignments also reverse without revising the convergence interpretation. These problems prevent a reliable judgment that the added comparisons produce a net quality improvement.
